text.p: The copper market's steep backwardation contracted slightly on Tuesday afternoon, and prices responded by sliding below $2,300 a tonne in whipsaw trading, dealers said. Copper's choppy behaviour was reflected throughout the base metals complex, with most London Metal Exchange (LME) metals ending the afternoon kerb in the minus column.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau index rose 0.64 points to 235.15.

Flagship three months copper came off an early high of $2,337 to finish just above the day's lows at $2,278, compared to Monday's kerb close of $2,315. The cash to threes backwardation, which flared by $100 during Third Wednesday pricing on Monday, ended the kerb little changed at $250/$255.
Zinc ended in the middle of the day's range, failing to recover back above the $1,500 level it achieved on Monday. It ended the kerb at $1,491, down $11.
Aluminium was also lower and dealers noted that trading was made difficult by uncertainty in copper. Kerb trading ended $21 lower at $1,563 per tonne.

Lead sustained a major drop, tumbling $20 to $638 after making strong upside progress earlier this month. Below $650 it hit sell stops, traders noted, but then it found some support at its 30-day moving average around $636.
Tin followed the others down $75 to $5,515 and alloy was off sharply at $1,415/$1,425, compared with $1,435/1,440.

COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures ended mostly lower Tuesday, after another intraday recovery ran out of steam near the close, but volumes remained moderate, and gold and silver held above recent contract lows. COMEX August gold ended down $1.80 at $319.00, as momentum indicators weakened again on intraday charts, and prices tested the bottom of the triangle consolidation pattern built up in the past week, after August gold saw a contract low at $314.60 last Monday. In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $318.00/50, compared to the London Tuesday afternoon fix at $319.75 and the New York close Monday around $319.70/10.

IPE Brent crude futures raced higher on Tuesday to close up 59 cents, backed by a rally in U.S. gasoline markets and underpinned by technical support, brokers said. August IPE Brent last traded at $18.41 a barrel, off seven cents from the day's high. The contract crept into backwardation against September, which last traded at $18.38, up 52 cents.

CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed higher, pulled up by a rally in corn futures, traders said. "There was spillover input from corn and harvest is winding down," said Dean Witter analyst Jerry Gidel. Corn was boosted by forecasts for hotter, drier weather in the U.S. Midwest which could interfere with that crop's key pollination stage of development. Dry weather in parts of Australia's wheat growing region also buoyed futures but fund buying was pitted against commercial selling, traders said.
